entry.title: Cosplaying as a founder at the Corgi Café in London
entry.content: The Corgi Café promises a 24-hour, laptop-friendly space for the grindset crowd in a city that's never been able to match Silicon Valley's startup buzz. I dropped by to see if London's tech scene has finally arrived. | Read full post >>

entry.title: We are witnessing the death of the games console
entry.content: Rising prices, diminishing generational leaps, and the slow death of physical media have stripped games consoles of their advantages. The days of PlayStation and Xbox as we know them may be numbered. | Read full post >>

entry.title: FIFA's failed sell-off and the duty of custodianship
entry.content: Gianni Infantino has scrapped his plan to sell stakes in FIFA's competitions, including the World Cup, to investors. It was always the wrong idea – custodians don't get to sell what they're only trusted to protect. | Read full post >>

entry.title: Will the RAM crunch force a return to optimisation?
entry.content: Software bloat went unchecked for decades because memory was cheap. Now it isn't, and consumers can't afford those same specs. Which way the industry turns next depends on values, not just technology. | Read full post >>

entry.title: Your new feature is clever — but does it work in real life?
entry.content: Great products are built for users – not to chase new trends, save a few extra pennies, or restrict customer choice. Sometimes what seem like good ideas to executives and designers simply don’t stand up in real life. | Read full post >>

entry.title: Alternatives to the UK government’s social media ban
entry.content: The UK government wants to ban social media for under-16s. The goal is reasonable, but there are more effective alternatives that don't require sacrificing privacy and anonymity for the rest of the population. | Read full post >>

entry.title: The UK government is quietly eroding online anonymity
entry.content: The Online Safety Act brought age checks to websites. Now the government wants them built into your devices – removing anonymity that protects whistleblowers, dissidents, and honest personal writing. | Read full post >>
